Measured code directly: grepped aria-*, role=, alt=, tabIndex counts across app/ and components/ (878 aria-* occurrences, 74 role=, 91 alt= of which 55 are alt="", only 10 tabIndex); counted div-onClick (7) vs button-onClick (232) vs total onClick (744); computed WCAG contrast ratios in Python for every ink/grey token against white and against s-bg-sunken; grepped for prefers-reduced-motion (41 hits, real coverage), skip-link (exists, SkipLink.tsx), landmark elements (<main>/<nav>/<header>/<footer> counts across app/ and specifically across all 49 dashboard page.tsx files), aria-live (10 hits total, 0 in the three search files), TabPill/PillToggle/FilterSheet for role/aria-selected/aria-pressed, react-aria usage in package.json, and eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y/axe-core presence in package.json and ~/.claude/hooks. Ran the required absence-proof greps for WCAG SC numbers, nFADP/BehiG/EAA, and focus-ring/contrast-minimum language across _design-system, _rules, _docs, CLAUDE.md, _backend-system and ~/.claude. Checked REMOVED.md and TASTE_LOG.md for prior kills before proposing anything.

findings.title: No visible focus indicator survives on any non-input control, and no substitute was ever mandated
findings.principle: Every focusable interactive element that is not a text input (link, button, pill, tab, icon-button, summary, [role=button], [tabindex]) must render a visible, non-color-only state change on :focus-visible with at least 3:1 contrast against its adjacent colors (WCAG 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured Minimum, and the base 2.4.7 Focus Visible, both AA). If a ring/outline stays banned for aesthetic reasons, ONE approved non-ring alternative (ink background fill, underline extension, or the border-color shift THE INPUT FOCUS LAW already uses for inputs) must be defined and wired globally for chrome elements the same way inputs already got one. A resting state of zero visible change on keyboard focus is never acceptable, ring or no ring.
findings.why: A sighted keyboard user (motor-impaired, or anyone tabbing instead of pointing) currently gets no signal of which link, button, pill, or tab is about to activate on the next Enter/Space press anywhere except a text input. That is not a smaller version of accessibility, it is its total absence on every button and link in the product.
findings.local_evidence: app/globals.css:387-393 sets `outline:none` unconditionally on `a:focus, a:focus-visible, button:focus, button:focus-visible, [role="button"]:focus-visible, [tabindex]:focus-visible, summary:focus-visible` for ALL devices (not touch-only; the touch-only carve-out is a separate, later block at :407-420). The code's own comment at :381-382 states plainly 'this drops the WCAG 2.4.7 keyboard focus indicator on chrome, owner call.' Only `input:focus-visible, textarea:focus-visible, select:focus-visible` (globals.css:1255-1264+) keep any focus treatment. The ONE a11y-adjacent enforcement hook in the whole estate, `~/.claude/hooks/no-focus-ring-gate.py`, exists to BLOCK re-adding a ring; there is no counterpart gate that requires any substitute indicator, so the estate's only automated a11y control currently enforces the ring's absence, not the requirement it replaces.
findings.absence_proof: grep -rin 'focus.appearance\|2.4.11\|2.4.13' _design-system _rules _docs CLAUDE.md _backend-system -> zero hits anywhere (only 2.4.7 is named, in RATIONALE.md and QUESTIONS.md, both describing the ORIGINAL ring that has since been deleted). grep -rn 'substitute focus\|focus fallback\|non-ring focus' -> zero hits. grep -rn 'no-focus-ring-gate' ~/.claude/hooks confirms the gate blocks additions, it does not require an alternative.
findings.existing_coverage: partial: SOURCE.md section 16.2 still asserts as current law 'Every interactive element MUST have focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:outline-s-ink...' and section 16's own anti-pattern list bans exactly what shipped ('Using outline: none without a replacement focus indicator'), and CLAUDE.md's design-contract 'focus' row still claims 'buttons/links: the global 2px ink outline' is live. RATIONALE.md:119 is the only place that honestly records the current state as 'a recorded owner tradeoff, not an oversight' for links/buttons specifically. The delta the existing text does not say: no doc anywhere prescribes what the REQUIRED substitute treatment is, and none of SOURCE/CLAUDE.md/LOCKFILE have been reconciled with the current CSS, so a future contributor reading section 16.2 or the CLAUDE.md contract row would ship believing a focus ring still exists.
findings.where_it_should_live: _design-system/SOURCE.md section 16.2 (rewrite to match shipped reality) plus app/globals.css (add the mandated non-ring substitute rule next to THE INPUT FOCUS LAW block)
findings.enforcement: gate:focus-indicator-presence-gate - a Playwright/axe check that tabs through a sample of interactive elements per page template and asserts a measurable style delta (background, border, or text-decoration) between resting and :focus-visible computed styles

findings.title: <html lang> is hardcoded to German across a de/en/fr/it site
findings.principle: The rendered `<html lang>` attribute must be set dynamically from the active `[locale]` route segment (de/en/fr/it) on every request, never hardcoded in the root layout. This is WCAG 3.1.1 Language of Page (A), and it governs how every screen reader picks its pronunciation, hyphenation, and voice for the entire page.
findings.why: A screen-reader user browsing the English, French, or Italian version of Solen (3 of the site's 4 shipped languages) currently has their assistive tech read the whole page using German phoneme rules, mangling pronunciation of every word on the page, not just a few labels.
findings.local_evidence: app/layout.tsx:39: `<html lang="de" className={...} suppressHydrationWarning>` is the single root `<html>` element for the whole app (there is no second `<html>` tag in app/[locale]/layout.tsx, confirmed by grep). `grep -rn "lang=" app/[locale]/layout.tsx` returns zero matches, and `grep -rn "document.documentElement.lang|htmlLang|setAttribute(.lang" app lib` returns zero matches anywhere in the codebase, so nothing ever overrides the hardcoded value at runtime for en/fr/it routes.
findings.absence_proof: grep -rin '3.1.1\|html lang=\|dynamic lang\|locale.*lang attribute' _design-system CLAUDE.md _docs _rules -> zero hits. SOURCE.md section 17 (i18n rules) and section 16 (Accessibility rules) were both read in full; neither mentions the html lang attribute at all.
findings.where_it_should_live: app/layout.tsx (read the locale param and set lang dynamically, or move the <html> tag into app/[locale]/layout.tsx) + a new _design-system/SOURCE.md section 17 line naming this explicitly
findings.enforcement: gate: a Playwright smoke check that loads /de, /en, /fr, /it and asserts document.documentElement.lang matches the URL locale

findings.title: Viewport meta disables pinch-zoom sitewide
findings.principle: Never set `maximumScale` below a value that blocks zoom, and never set `userScalable: false`, on any page's viewport meta. Structural-UI protection against accidental pinch-zoom belongs on the specific gesture-sensitive element (`touch-action` CSS on a map or gallery), never on the document-level viewport, because disabling the OS pinch gesture for the whole page is WCAG 1.4.4 Resize Text (AA) technique failure F102, and it removes the ONLY zoom mechanism low-vision users on Android Chrome have (iOS Safari has ignored the flag since iOS 10, so this bites Android specifically, silently).
findings.why: A low-vision user on the largest global mobile OS by device count needs pinch-zoom to read anything the site's own text-size scale does not already cover; disabling it removes their only fallback, and the comment justifying it (preventing 'accidental pinch-zoom' on the structural grid) is solved elsewhere in the same file with `touch-action` on individual elements, so the sitewide block buys nothing the local fix didn't already cover.
findings.local_evidence: app/layout.tsx:29-32: `export const viewport: Viewport = { width: "device-width", initialScale: 1, maximumScale: 1, userScalable: false, viewportFit: "cover" }`. The adjacent comment (lines 24-28) explicitly frames this as intentional: 'maximumScale=1 + userScalable=false locks the structural UI... Content pinch-zoom on specific elements (photos, maps) still works via touch-action: pinch-zoom on those elements if needed' - i.e. the codebase already has the correct narrow-scope tool and used the wrong, page-wide one anyway.
findings.absence_proof: grep -rin 'userScalable\|maximumScale\|user-scalable\|maximum-scale\|pinch.zoom\|zoom.disab' _design-system CLAUDE.md _docs -> only the two hits inside app/layout.tsx itself (the comment and the value); RATIONALE.md's two 1.4.4 mentions are both about rem-based spacing scaling honoring OS font-size, a different mechanism, never about the viewport zoom lock. No doc reconciles this as an accepted risk.
findings.where_it_should_live: app/layout.tsx (remove maximumScale/userScalable, keep touch-action on the specific map/gallery elements) + _design-system/SOURCE.md section 16.4 or a new subsection
findings.enforcement: gate: a static check on app/layout.tsx and any other viewport export that fails the build if userScalable is false or maximumScale < 5

findings.title: The dashboard has no accessibility floor at all: zero landmarks, two-thirds of pages carry zero ARIA
findings.principle: Every dashboard/admin page ships the SAME landmark and ARIA floor a customer page must: exactly one `<main>` wrapping the page content, the sidebar rendered as `<nav aria-label="...">` (not a bare `<div>`), and every icon-only control carrying `aria-label`, checked and enforced identically to customer screens. 'It's internal, salon owners aren't disabled' is not a valid exemption: dashboard staff are real end users, this is a Swiss employer-facing product surface, and internal tools are exactly the surfaces WCAG-adjacent audits (and, in the EU, the workplace-equipment provisions of the EAA) do NOT carve out.
findings.why: Every existing accessibility rule in this estate (SOURCE.md section 16, the CLAUDE.md design contract, the FLOORS LAW) is written and measured against 'customer screens' only. The dashboard is a 49-page surface that salon owners and staff, some of whom are older, some of whom may use assistive tech, operate every single day to run their business, and it has been built with none of the same care.
findings.local_evidence: `grep -rl "<main" app/[locale]/dashboard --include="page.tsx"` returns 0 of 49 dashboard page.tsx files. `grep -rln "<nav" app/[locale]/dashboard app/[locale]/_components/dashboard` returns zero files (no sidebar nav landmark exists anywhere). `grep -rlE 'aria-'` across the same 49-page dashboard tree returns only 16 files (67% of dashboard pages, 33 of 49, carry not one single aria-* attribute), despite 267 counted `onClick=` handlers across app/[locale]/dashboard.
findings.absence_proof: grep -rin 'dashboard.*accessib\|internal.*a11y\|owner.facing.*wcag\|admin.*landmark' _design-system CLAUDE.md _docs _rules -> zero hits. SOURCE.md section 16.1 landmarks rule says only 'Every page MUST have <main>... already in app/[locale]/layout.tsx' - that root layout wraps the top-level shell, but individual dashboard page.tsx files render their own content trees inside it without ever nesting a page-level <main>, and nothing in the doc scopes the rule to customer vs internal routes, meaning the rule was written assuming universal coverage that measurably does not exist on dashboard.
findings.existing_coverage: partial: SOURCE.md section 16.1 states the landmark requirement in general terms ('Every page MUST have...'), but names only customer components (Header/Footer/MobileMenu) as examples and was never checked against the dashboard tree; CLAUDE.md's entire taste-rules and FLOORS-LAW blocks are explicitly scoped to 'customer screen' language throughout, leaving dashboard with no equivalent floor by omission, not by a stated exemption.
findings.where_it_should_live: _design-system/COMPONENT_REGISTRY.md (a DashboardShell/DashboardLayout entry that owns <main> + <nav aria-label> once, centrally) and a new CLAUDE.md line explicitly extending the a11y floor to dashboard
findings.enforcement: gate: a lint rule or Playwright landmark-count check run against every app/[locale]/dashboard/*/page.tsx, failing if a rendered page has zero <main> ancestor

findings.title: No contrast-ratio gate exists, and the system has already authorized a sub-threshold grey for informational text
findings.principle: No text color token may be authorized for use on prose, labels, timestamps, hints, or placeholders below a computed 4.5:1 contrast ratio against its target background (3:1 only for text at or above 18pt/24px or 14pt/18.5px bold, per WCAG 1.4.3 AA). The contrast ratio must be computed and recorded in the SAME commit that authorizes a token for text use, not asserted from vibes. A token that fails 4.5:1 is restricted by definition to genuinely non-text use (dividers, disabled-icon fills) that 1.4.3 exempts, and that restriction must be written into the token's own row, not left to a component author's judgment call at build time.
findings.why: 'Non-load-bearing' is not a WCAG exemption category: a timestamp, a placeholder, or a hint is still text a sighted low-vision user needs to read, and 1.4.3 does not distinguish 'important' text from 'hint' text, only text from decoration. Authorizing a color this far under threshold for exactly the text types (timestamps, hints, placeholders) users most often squint at is backwards.
findings.local_evidence: Computed directly: contrast(#9CA3AF, #FFFFFF) = 2.54:1, contrast(#9CA3AF, #F4F4F5) = 2.31:1, both far under the 4.5:1 AA floor and even under the 3:1 large-text floor. CLAUDE.md's FLOORS LAW block (the pinned block in this very repo's root CLAUDE.md, display-anchor row) states: 'Tertiary grey #9CA3AF (s-chart-2) is reinstated for NON-load-bearing text only (chevrons, placeholders, timestamps, hints)... forbidden on load-bearing copy' - i.e. the estate's own live governing doc explicitly authorizes 2.54:1 grey for exactly the text categories 1.4.3 does not exempt. Current usage is 0 (`grep -rn 'text-s-chart-2' app components` -> 0 hits), so this has not shipped live yet, but the law is armed and would ship an inaccessible token the next time someone builds a timestamp or hint using it, believing it's sanctioned.
findings.absence_proof: grep -rin 'contrast.*4.5\|contrast.*minimum\|contrast.gate\|contrast-ratio' _design-system CLAUDE.md _rules _docs -> only SOURCE.md section 16.4, a static table of 6 pre-existing pairings computed once on 2026-05-26 with no re-check mechanism and no coverage of tokens introduced since (s-chart-2 postdates it). grep -rn 'contrast' ~/.claude/hooks -> zero hits, confirming no automated check exists anywhere in the hook estate despite ~130 other enforcement hooks.
findings.existing_coverage: partial: SOURCE.md section 16.4 documents contrast ratios for the ORIGINAL token set as a one-time table, correctly computed for those pairs, but it is not a gate, has never been re-run against tokens added later (s-ink-2/#6B6B6B is fine at 5.33:1, s-chart-2/#9CA3AF is not and was never checked against it), and LOCKFILE.md's own s-chart-2 definition scopes it to 'bar/line/area charts' ONLY, which the CLAUDE.md FLOORS LAW block then contradicts by re-authorizing it for prose. The delta: no mechanism catches a future token or a future rule that reopens a failing color for text.
findings.where_it_should_live: _design-system/LOCKFILE.md token table (add a computed-contrast column per token, on white AND on s-bg-sunken) + reconcile the CLAUDE.md FLOORS LAW s-chart-2 line against LOCKFILE's chart-only scope
findings.enforcement: gate:token-contrast-gate - a script that computes WCAG contrast for every color token against its documented usage backgrounds and fails if any token authorized for text use scores under 4.5:1 (3:1 for a documented large-text exception)

findings.title: Salon photography has no alt-text content policy; portfolio images are blanket-marked decorative
findings.principle: Alt text on salon and portfolio photography must describe the photographic content relevant to a booking decision (hairstyle, cut length, color technique, interior style) in the salon's own words or a structured template drawing on actual photo metadata, never a bare index ('Salon Name – 1') or a generic filler phrase ('Foto von {name}'). A portfolio/gallery image whose entire on-screen purpose is customer evaluation (a haircut result, a stylist's past work) is NEVER marked `alt=""`; only chrome, pattern, or purely repeated-elsewhere images qualify as decorative under WCAG 1.1.1.
findings.why: Alt text that just numbers or names a photo conveys nothing a screen-reader user can act on when the entire point of a portfolio gallery is to help a sighted user evaluate a hairstyle before booking; a blind or low-vision user is given the same purchase-decision surface as everyone else but with the content stripped out and replaced by a counter.
findings.local_evidence: app/[locale]/_components/salon/SalonImageGallery.tsx:232: `` (alt text is literally just the salon name plus a photo index, describing nothing about the photo). app/[locale]/_components/homepage/SalonCard.tsx:431: `alt={photoAlt ?? \`Foto von ${name}\`}` (fallback is 'Photo of {name}', equally generic). Separately, `_design-system/_pending-migration.md` shows a recurring pattern of portfolio/lightbox images shipped with `alt=""` (e.g. lines 56337-56361, the portfolio lightbox, and line 56524, a portfolio thumbnail `p.photo_url`), marking genuinely evaluative content as decorative.
findings.absence_proof: grep -rin 'alt text\|alt-text\|alternative text\|alt policy' _design-system CLAUDE.md _docs -> zero hits outside the raw code samples inside _pending-migration.md (a migration scratch file, not a rule doc). SOURCE.md section 9 (Photography & user content under B&W lock) was read in full and covers color treatment of photos only, never alt text.
findings.where_it_should_live: _design-system/SOURCE.md section 9 (Photography) or a new section 16.3 sub-bullet + components/SalonImageGallery.md
findings.enforcement: checklist (content policy, not mechanically checkable without photo-understanding); a lint CAN at least flag any alt prop that is a template literal containing only a name/index variable with no other static or dynamic descriptive text

findings.title: Tab-like selection controls (TabPill) expose their selected state only through color and weight, never through role or ARIA state
findings.principle: Any control letting a user pick one option from a visible set exposes that selection programmatically, not only visually: `role="tablist"`/`role="tab"` + `aria-selected` for navigational content tabs (the pattern CLAUDE.md's own design-contract 'selected/active' row names as 'CONTENT TABS'), or `role="radiogroup"`/`aria-pressed` on a group for a filter/segment picker, matching the pattern PillToggle already implements correctly for the same visual family. A background-fill or font-weight change with no role/state attribute fails WCAG 4.1.2 Name Role Value and SOURCE.md's own anti-pattern list.
findings.why: A screen-reader user tabbing through a TabPill-based content-tab strip or sort-segment control hears only 'button, Buchungen' and 'button, Termine' with no indication which one is currently active; the sighted-only cue (grey fill + semibold) is invisible to them, so they cannot tell what content they're already looking at.
findings.local_evidence: `grep -n 'role=\|aria-selected\|aria-controls' app/[locale]/_components/primitives/TabPill.tsx app/[locale]/_components/profile/ProfileTabs.tsx app/[locale]/_components/salon/SalonStickyTabNav.tsx` returns zero matches across all three files. By contrast, the sibling primitive `PillToggle.tsx` DOES correctly implement `role={...}` and `aria-pressed={active}` (lines 56-61) for its own multi/single-select pattern, showing the codebase already knows the correct pattern and simply didn't apply it to TabPill.
findings.absence_proof: grep -rin 'role="tab"\|aria-selected\|tablist' app components -> zero hits anywhere in the codebase; no tab-role pattern exists at all despite CLAUDE.md's own design contract naming a 'CONTENT TABS' component ('title + 2px ink underline, active = 600 ink + underline, inactive = 400 ink-2, no fill').
findings.existing_coverage: partial: SOURCE.md section 16.3 and its anti-pattern list ('Color as the ONLY signal of state') already state the general principle; the gap is that TabPill itself, the concrete component the rule should bind, was never brought into compliance, and no registry entry for TabPill (COMPONENT_REGISTRY.md) mentions ARIA at all.
findings.enforcement: gate: a lint check flagging any component rendering >1 sibling button/div with a shared 'active index' prop pattern that lacks aria-selected or aria-pressed

findings.title: No live-region announcement when search results re-render on filter/keystroke
findings.principle: Any surface that re-renders a result COUNT or list in place, without a page navigation, in response to a filter change or keystroke (search, filter sheet, sort) must expose the change to assistive tech via a single `aria-live="polite"` region announcing the new state (e.g. '24 Ergebnisse gefunden'), separate from the visually-rendered count, so a screen-reader user is told the list changed instead of having to re-discover it by re-navigating the whole result grid.
findings.why: A sighted user filtering search results sees the count and cards update instantly; a screen-reader user tabbing through the same filter controls gets total silence and has to manually re-traverse the entire results region after every interaction to find out whether anything changed, which is exactly the kind of invisible-to-sighted-review gap this project's own 'silent no-op' framing was built to catch in backend filters.
findings.local_evidence: `grep -n 'aria-live' app/[locale]/_components/search/SearchTemplate.tsx app/[locale]/_components/search/SearchOverlay.tsx app/[locale]/_components/search/FilterSheet.tsx` returns zero matches across all three files, the entire search/filter surface. SearchTemplate.tsx does carry a `resultCount={total}` prop (line 2045) proving the live count is already computed and available, it is simply never wired to an aria-live region alongside its visual render.
findings.absence_proof: The only 10 aria-live occurrences in the whole app/ + components/ tree (grepped) are in booking/lookup, booking/resend-link, HeartButton, OfflineBanner, FieldHelper, WelcomeToast, Toast, and Textarea, none of them the search/discovery surface that is the product's primary interaction loop. grep -rin 'live region\|aria-live' _design-system CLAUDE.md -> SOURCE.md section 16.3 mentions aria-live only as an example for 'save toggles', never for search/filter result updates.
findings.existing_coverage: partial: SOURCE.md section 16.3 establishes the general aria-live principle for dynamic content, but scopes its own example to save-toggle feedback only, and no rule or example ever names search-result-count as a required live region, so the biggest dynamic-content surface in the product was never brought under the existing rule's umbrella.
findings.where_it_should_live: app/[locale]/_components/search/SearchTemplate.tsx (a single sr-only aria-live region wrapping the result-count string) + _design-system/SOURCE.md section 16.3 (name search/filter explicitly as a required live-region surface)
findings.enforcement: checklist / manual verification (screen-reader spot check with VoiceOver on a filter change); mechanically, a lint rule requiring any component consuming a `resultCount`/`total` prop to also render an aria-live sibling

findings.title: No automated accessibility lint or scan exists anywhere in a 130-plus-gate estate
findings.principle: Ship eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y (or an equivalent axe-core/@axe-core/playwright CI scan) as a BLOCKING gate, wired the same way drift-check, type-budget, and no-focus-ring already are: run on every PR/build, fail on new violations, with an explicit suppression file for pre-existing debt so it does not become a wall of red on day one.
findings.why: This estate enforces color drift, type-scale budgets, motion durations, and dead-click contracts with dedicated blocking hooks, but has zero automated check for the one category (accessibility) with actual legal exposure attached (the estate's own PSYCH_BUSINESS_IMPACT.md research already names rising ADA-style digital accessibility lawsuits as a live risk category for ecommerce). Every other domain graduated from 'advice' to 'gate' specifically because, per this project's own stated doctrine, advice gets outranked under task focus and a gate doesn't; accessibility is the one domain that never made that jump.
findings.local_evidence: `grep -n 'eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y\|axe-core\|@axe-core\|pa11y\|lighthouse' package.json` returns zero matches. `ls ~/.claude/hooks | grep -i 'a11y\|access\|contrast\|focus'` returns exactly one file, `no-focus-ring-gate.py`, and (per finding accessibility-01) that gate enforces the ABSENCE of a focus indicator, not the presence of accessibility semantics; it is not an accessibility-positive check by function. By contrast the same hooks directory carries dedicated gates for white-only-web, no-decorative-image, reference-measure, type-budget, and dozens of other narrower design concerns.
findings.absence_proof: grep -rin 'jsx-a11y\|axe-core\|a11y lint\|a11y gate\|a11y ci' _design-system CLAUDE.md _rules _docs ~/.claude/*.md -> zero hits anywhere.
findings.where_it_should_live: package.json devDependencies + eslint config + a new ~/.claude/hooks/a11y-lint-gate (or CI workflow step) + a line in this project's CLAUDE.md ship-gates section alongside SENIOR_SCORECARD.md
findings.enforcement: gate:a11y-lint-gate (eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y as a blocking PR check; axe-core Playwright scan on the 5-10 highest-traffic customer routes as a second layer)

findings.title: Swiss/EU accessibility legal exposure is named nowhere despite the estate already tracking the adjacent US risk
findings.principle: Record, in one place, which WCAG conformance level Solen is actually targeting (this audit finds no such statement anywhere) and name the two statutes that actually bind a Swiss marketplace serving EU customers: Switzerland's BehiG (Behindertengleichstellungsgesetz, federal digital-service accessibility duties) and the EU's European Accessibility Act (EN 301 549 / WCAG 2.1 AA baseline, in force for covered digital services since June 2025) if Solen ever serves EU-domiciled customers or expands there. This is a compliance-tracking gap, not a design-system rule, and belongs in a dated decision record, not silently assumed.
findings.why: The estate already tracks the analogous US risk qualitatively (rising ADA-style digital accessibility lawsuits against ecommerce, sourced) in its own psychology-business-impact research, so the pattern of naming legal exposure by source already exists; it simply was never extended to the jurisdictions Solen actually operates in.
findings.local_evidence: _design-system/research/PSYCH_BUSINESS_IMPACT.md:169 already contains: 'ADA-style digital accessibility lawsuits rising, target ecommerce, overlays don't prevent suits | [UsableNet/Ecomback]... | fix native contrast/labels, don't rely on an overlay widget | medium' - proving the estate has the exact right instinct and sourcing discipline for this category, aimed at the wrong country.
findings.absence_proof: grep -rin 'nFADP\|behig\|swiss.*accessib\|accessibility law\|legal exposure\|EAA\|European Accessibility Act' _design-system _rules _docs CLAUDE.md -> zero hits for BehiG or EAA anywhere in the entire estate; the only nFADP hits in the whole repo are about DATA-retention compliance (_docs/BACKEND.md), an unrelated statute, not digital accessibility.
findings.where_it_should_live: _design-system/research/PSYCH_BUSINESS_IMPACT.md (extend the existing ADA-lawsuit row) or a new _rules/ACCESSIBILITY_COMPLIANCE.md naming the target conformance level and the two statutes
findings.enforcement: doc-only (this is a record-keeping/risk-tracking principle, not a mechanically enforceable one)
